headline: President accepts Ishraque Hossain’s resignation as state minister
summary: The state minister for Liberation War Affairs stepped down following backlash over a video showing him brandishing a firearm during an anti-drug drive.
details: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has formally accepted the resignation of Ishraque Hossain, the state minister for Liberation War Affairs, as confirmed by a Cabinet Division gazette notification.

The resignation follows a controversial video that spread on social media showing the Dhaka-6 lawmaker brandishing a firearm and using force against ordinary people during an 'anti-drug drive' in Gandaria, Dhaka.
Following the incident, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman spoke to Ishraque and asked him to resign after a cabinet meeting on Sunday afternoon.
At a press conference at the Jatiya Press Club, Ishraque stated he had voluntarily resigned to protect the party's image and uphold its honour, claiming he had used the weapon in self-defence.
With his exit, the government now consists of 23 state ministers and 27 full ministers, including the prime Minister.
Ishraque is the third minister to leave the eight-month-old government, following the resignations of Dipen Dewan and Zahir Uddin Swapon.
caption:
A state minister resigns after a video shows him brandishing a firearm during a drug raid.

President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has formally accepted the resignation of Ishraque Hossain, the state minister for Liberation War Affairs, as confirmed by a Cabinet Division gazette notification.

The resignation follows a controversial video that spread on social media showing the Dhaka-6 lawmaker brandishing a firearm and using force against ordinary people during an 'anti-drug drive' in Gandaria, Dhaka.

Following the incident, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman spoke to Ishraque and asked him to resign after a cabinet meeting on Sunday afternoon.

At a press conference at the Jatiya Press Club, Ishraque stated he had voluntarily resigned to protect the party's image and uphold its honour, claiming he had used the weapon in self-defence.

With his exit, the government now consists of 23 state ministers and 27 full ministers, including the prime Minister.

Ishraque is the third minister to leave the eight-month-old government, following the resignations of Dipen Dewan and Zahir Uddin Swapon.

headline_marked: PM Tarique: [[Religion should not be a barrier]] to building Bangladesh
headline: PM Tarique: Religion should not be a barrier to building Bangladesh
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for unity among all religious communities, stating that "religion is for individuals, the state is for everyone." He emphasized equal rights and dignity for all citizens.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed his hope that religion will not create any barriers between people. He stated, "Religion is for individuals, the state is for everyone." The Prime Minister made these remarks during a roadside rally in Taraganj, Rangpur, while on his way to visit a Sharadiya Durgapuja pandal.

"We are all Bangladeshis. We have grown up on the soil of this country. We are Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, and Christian – religion is for each of us, but the country belongs to all of us. This country is ours, and we all have rights to it. Every citizen of this country must be ensured equal dignity and rights," he added.

Tarique Rahman urged all religious communities to unite and move the country forward. "Our expectation is that we will build a beautiful Bangladesh bound by the ties of harmony, amity, and fraternity," he said.

Earlier in the day, the Prime Minister traveled by military aircraft to Syedpur Airport and then proceeded by road towards Rangpur. Around 11 AM, he stopped at Taraganj's Chowpothi area, dismounted from his vehicle, and addressed a roadside rally organized by local BNP leaders. His speech lasted approximately one and a half to two minutes.

Later, while en route to Rangpur city, he also addressed a roadside rally in Paglapir. There, he mentioned that various public welfare activities have been initiated since the election victory to stand by the people. A "Family Card" has been launched for the welfare of the general public, and a "Farmer Card" for farmers. Initiatives have also been taken to ensure the welfare of Imams, Muezzins, and religious leaders of other faiths.
The Prime Minister stated, "Our goal is to stand by people from all walks of life and build a beautiful, prosperous, and egalitarian Bangladesh."

Tarique Rahman recalled that during the Great Liberation War, people of all religions, including Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, and Christian, fought shoulder-to-shoulder to liberate the country. "It is through their collective sacrifice and struggle that we have achieved our beloved Bangladesh."

Expressing his hope for strengthening the bonds of unity, love, and harmony among people of all religions, the Prime Minister said, "People of the country, irrespective of religion and ethnicity, should be able to live safely, practice their respective religions freely, and participate in the country's development with equal dignity."

The Prime Minister entered the Radhagobinda Temple's puja pandal, located in front of the Press Club in Rangpur city, at 12:04 PM. Temple committee members welcomed him. Local media personnel were not allowed inside the temple.

The temple committee members expressed their joy at the Prime Minister's visit, which had generated excitement among committee members and visitors for several days. Extensive security arrangements were in place around the temple and at the city's entry points.
